key_insight: Pixel MeanFlow (pMF) enables one-step, latent-free image generation by separating what the network predicts (output space) from how it's trained (loss space), allowing a single-step flow transform from simple noise to high-quality images.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between multi-step latent diffusion/flow models and fully one-step, pixel-space generative models — removing iterative sampling and latent-space dependencies that increase latency and system complexity.
method: Design a flow-based generator whose network outputs live in a tailored pixel-space (the "mean flow" representation) while the optimization/loss is computed in the target image space.
Train the model so a single transformation maps simple base noise directly to images (one-step sampling) without intermediate latents or multi-step denoising.
Separate output & loss spaces to stabilize training and align the model's predictive target with perceptual/image reconstruction objectives.
impact: Practitioners get a fast, simpler alternative to multi-step diffusion/flow pipelines — enabling real-time or resource-constrained image synthesis and easier deployment while retaining high image quality.
visual_elements: High-level pipeline diagram: single-step mapping from noise to image, highlighting separation between network output space and loss space.

paper_title: One-step Latent-free Image Generation with Pixel Mean Flows
paper_authors: Yiyang Lu, Susie Lu, Qiao Sun, Hanhong Zhao, Zhicheng Jiang
